title: Taking rhythm and blues jobs in the 1950s as just work
summary: He worked with r&b groups and singers like Hadda Brooks as a job for pay, recalling how as a boy he gave party money to his parents.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, so in other words, -- how did you feel, like in the '50s -- I know in the '60s you were working with the Ink Spots and a few other people like that, playing, you know, lead guitar.
Uh-huh.
But in the '50s you worked a lot with some rhythm and blues type groups.
Yeah.
And blues singers, like Hattie Brooks and so forth. Some of that music was pretty simple, compared to some of the jazz that you played.
Yeah.
How did you feel about that?
Well, I just wanted to make that money, (Unintelligible) that's all.
I mean musically, did you feel you were wasting your time in a way?

No, I didn't. I'd think, every time I'd go on a job like that, just like recording with Hatia Brooks, I just felt like it was a record date I had to do, and I might as well go ahead and make that money for it, because it does me some good when I got the money for it that I'd worked for.
And that was your -- you thought of it as a job.
That's right.
You're a musician, so if it's music you go do it.
Yeah. It was a job, so I went on and did it.
Uh-huh.
Got my money and forgot about it.
Uh-huh.
To tell you the truth, I didn't think I was going to be in this kind of situation, like all I knew was that I could play the guitar.
Yeah.
You know. But I didn't know how great it was. Things would come up like you're doing today.
Yeah.
And others that has done it.
Uh-huh.
You know what I mean. I didn't think I'd ever be in that.
You were just trying to play the instrument the best you could.
I just tried to play the instrument to please me.
Uh-huh.
I'd go on parties and get hired for a party, a house party, like them social functions.
Uh-huh.

And I'd make $12 and $14.00 a night, and come home, I'd give the money to my father and mother, and they'd give me a couple of dollars, and I'd give them the rest and they'd run the house with it. In other words, I took care of the family, with what I was doing.
That must have been very satisfying.
Yeah.
